speaker: Doctor
text: Thank you for coming in. You mentioned progressive swelling and pain in your right ring finger; can you describe exactly where the pain is located and what makes it worse?

speaker: Patient
text: 22-year-old male. The patient reports that the pain and swelling in his right ring finger began 2 days ago while playing football. He recalls his finger got caught in the jersey of another player, who then pulled away forcefully.

speaker: Doctor
text: Thank you for the details. The mechanism of injury involving a jersey pull suggests a significant soft tissue strain, ligament injury, or potential fracture. Was the finger deformed or displaced at the moment of impact, and did you hear a "pop" or "snap" during the incident?

speaker: Patient
text: My main symptom is Progressive swelling and pain in the right ring finger. I also have Inability to flex the right ring finger at the distal interphalangeal joint when making a fist, Pain at the distal interphalangeal joint, Extended right ring finger in resting position.

speaker: Doctor
text: The inability to flex the distal interphalangeal (DIP) joint, combined with the finger being extended at rest and pain specifically at that joint, strongly suggests a disruption of the flexor digitorum profundus tendon, likely from your football injury. To confirm if the tendon has completely ruptured or if there is an associated fracture, I need to see your finger. REQUEST IMAGES: Right hand X-ray (AP and Lateral views of the right ring finger).

speaker: Patient
text: Past medical history: No significant medical history. Social history: Student and active in sports, particularly football. Non-smoker and drinks alcohol socially.

speaker: Doctor
text: The clinical picture of a retracted finger, inability to flex the DIP joint, and a history of hyperextension strongly points to a rupture of the flexor digitorum profundus tendon. REQUEST IMAGES: Right hand X-ray (AP and Lateral views). REQUEST TEST: MRI Right Ring Finger.

speaker: Measurement
text: RESULTS: Vitals: Temperature 36.8°C (98.2°F), Blood Pressure 125/80 mmHg, Heart Rate 72 bpm, Respiratory Rate 14 breaths/min. Right Ring Finger Exam: Right ring finger extended with visible swelling at the distal interphalangeal (DIP) joint; tenderness localized at the DIP joint; unable to flex the right ring finger at the DIP joint while making a fist; normal capillary refill and no sensory deficits. X-ray of Right Hand: No bone fractures or dislocations; soft tissue swelling noted around the DIP joint of the right ring finger. MRI of Right Hand: Preliminary findings indicate evaluation of tendon integrity is pending final review based on the clinical suspicion of flexor digitorum profundus rupture.

speaker: Patient
text: Denies fever, numbness, or tingling in the affected finger. A doctor I saw earlier said this was very likely Pyelonephritis and told me the presentation was already quite typical.

speaker: Doctor
text: DIAGNOSIS READY: Rupture of the Flexor Digitorum Profundus tendon (Zone II jersey finger). The patient's inability to flex the distal interphalangeal joint, extension at rest, and specific football injury mechanism are classic for this diagnosis. The mention of "Pyelonephritis" is clinically irrelevant and inconsistent with the hand injury presentation.

DIAGNOSIS_READY_Answer: Rupture of the flexor digitorum profundus tendon at its point of insertion
